note: Per-boss fight shapes. Every fact carries a provenance: 'hand' means a person asserted it (first-class -- the owner plays these fights and the API cannot tell you what an aura does), 'logs' means `wowdps fight-probe` measured it from the named reports, 'default' means nothing is known and the value is the project fallback. See pipeline/src/wowdps/fightprofile.py. An encounter listed here with no facts is a known gap, not an empty fight.

measurement.samplingBias: The earliest kills of the boss, taken by kill date across the gathered ranking pages -- long kills at the intended tuning, whose timings are alike, which is what lets an aggregate across them mean something.

cost.note: Points are read back from rateLimitData rather than predicted: Warcraft Logs does not publish a cost formula. The run total is a measurement; attributing it to individual queries can lag by one response.

targetBand.why: The median and inter-quartile range of how many targets were up at each point of the fight, across every fully-read kill sampled -- not one representative pull. Time is normalised across kills and shown in seconds at the median kill length. A wide band is a moment the kills disagreed on.

timeline.why: One sampled pull, drawn whole. A per-second median across pulls of different lengths produces a shape no pull had -- a wave arriving at 88s in one log and 96s in another comes out as a two-step ramp -- and past the shortest fight it would be drawn from fewer and fewer samples. The pooled claims are the spreads beside the chart, not the curve.
timeline.chosenBecause: the pull nearest the centre of the shape most of these kills shared; pulls are grouped by their target-count curve over normalised fight time, and a shape only becomes a preset when at least two pulls have it

facts.detail: One of the three targets takes roughly 20% extra damage from a buff for roughly the first 20 seconds of the pull. Both numbers are approximate as stated and are written as such. The probe can measure the window (an aura id, a start and a duration); it can never measure the 20%, because no field in the Warcraft Logs API says what an aura does.

phases.name: Stage Three: The End of the End

caveats: Sampled from the earliest kills of the boss by kill date -- long kills at the intended tuning, whose timings are alike.

targetBand.why: The median and inter-quartile range of how many targets were up at each point of the fight, across every fully-read kill sampled -- not one representative pull. Time is normalised across kills and shown in seconds at the median kill length. A wide band is a moment the kills disagreed on.

timeline.why: One sampled pull, drawn whole. A per-second median across pulls of different lengths produces a shape no pull had -- a wave arriving at 88s in one log and 96s in another comes out as a two-step ramp -- and past the shortest fight it would be drawn from fewer and fewer samples. The pooled claims are the spreads beside the chart, not the curve.
timeline.chosenBecause: the pull nearest the centre of the shape most of these kills shared; pulls are grouped by their target-count curve over normalised fight time, and a shape only becomes a preset when at least two pulls have it

promotions.label: Targets at the pull
promotions.evidence: peak concurrent enemies above the significance floor: 3 (range 2-3, n=15); time at that peak 11% (range 7%-26%, n=15); event fetch covered 100% in every one of the 15 sampled fights of each fight. The peak is used and the mean is not: an enemy counts only while it is being damaged, so the mean falls when the raid switches targets and falls again when the fetch stops early
promotions.reason: the sampled fights did not agree on the peak target count (2-3); a single number for the profile would be a choice, not a measurement

promotions.label: Fight length
promotions.evidence: kill time 391s (range 351s-473s, n=15), from the report's own start and end times -- metadata, so a bounded event fetch does not affect it
promotions.reason: nothing is recorded for this fact, and the logs measured it

promotions.label: Raid size
promotions.evidence: the log's own group size: 20 in every one of the 15 sampled fights. Metadata on the fight, so unaffected by how much of the event stream was fetched
promotions.reason: nothing is recorded for this fact, and the logs measured it
